---
title: "Teaching"
---

My goal as a teacher is to prepare students to study, navigate, and shape the communication environments in which people make decisions about their health. I anchor concepts in real problems, real data, and real settings; keep the classroom welcoming and encouraging; and cultivate systems thinking, so students can reason about communication as a multilevel system in which message features, network structures, channel affordances, and social and political context jointly shape what spreads, what people believe, and what they do. My courses run on collaborative problem-solving, peer teaching, and structured discussion, culminating in projects where students apply course concepts to data and questions of their choice.

## Health communication training

Beyond the classroom, I teach health communication skills to early-career researchers, including a Society for Epidemiologic Research career-development webinar (2025) and a Harvard-affiliated writing retreat for early-stage investigators (2026). See [Talks](talks.qmd).
